candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0159.

options.A: These foods are recommended because aging lowers tyramine enough to prevent clinically important MAOI interactions during treatment.
options.B: Avoid high-tyramine aged or fermented foods because their interaction with phenelzine can precipitate a dangerous hypertensive crisis.
options.C: Eat the foods only with an antacid because reduced gastric acidity prevents tyramine absorption and makes the interaction clinically insignificant.
options.D: Skip phenelzine on the day of the event because one missed dose reliably removes the interaction risk while allowing unrestricted food choices.

candidate.rationale: Phenelzine labeling warns that tyramine-rich foods, including aged cheeses and dry/cured sausages, can precipitate hypertensive crises during MAOI therapy. Dietary restrictions cannot be made safe by skipping a single dose or taking an antacid.
